charter:
# Charter — T18 The real V2 UI (retrospective, 2026-11-24)

- **Project:** T18 'The real V2 UI', track v2, ADM phase G, capability plateau, tranche 4, project `01a20c80-b734-748a-b299-879ea19be681`, programme `01a1d039-0d24-7d16-ae52-4841e96ccfac`, plan `docs/plans/T18-real-v2-ui.md` (SPEC_V2 §10.5 and §12 T18). At the rework snapshot the project row is `status: active` (version 1, created 2026-11-24T07:41:22Z) with `meta.measured_status: proposed`, `meta.plan_status: draft`, `meta.issues: [559, 562, 563, 564, 565, 566]`, `meta.tranche: 4` and `meta.plateau: capability`.
- **Tranche and governance:** tranche 4 (`01a1e9e0-f4c0-727d-9afb-bb5b1e9783ce`, state authorised) was authorised at 2026-11-24T17:04:34Z by the tranche-3 review `01a20e84-325b-7fef-8f40-50b5e53550e9` (decision continue); the tranche-4 refinement `01a202a2-2705-7392-a2d1-03ca2b3a174e` records the WSJF inputs 9/7/10/5, and the tranche-4 PI cadence `01a202a1-dbb9-7e49-b64a-cf97c3fab095` lists T18 in its capacity. This charter is written by the 2026-11-24 retrospective rework under the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`.
- **Mandate:** make every V2 destination a real route in `apps/web` — the one Leptos CSR/WASM application served by the same binary on port 8930 — with its screen module, read/write contract, honest empty, error, happy and refusal states and a Playwright spec, while the design pack remains the public programme site at `/design/` and the reviewed reference (D64/D65).
- **Scope:** the shell, route registry and navigation; the ten V2 destinations of SPEC_V2 §10.5 (organisation, procedures, authoring, portfolio, programme, architecture, plan, improve, operations, tools) and the execution room; the L1–L4 delivery view; the V2 coverage instrument measured from real routes and specs; the T12 organisation loop. Out of scope: new tables, actions, events or ports; SSR; a second router or frontend; a mobile app; retiring the V1 routes or the design pack; and any production fixture.
- **Expected outputs:** `project-brief`, `inception-analysis` and `architecture-design`; the closure outputs `evidence` and `closure-review` remain unwritten because the project stays active.
- **What this retrospective does NOT attest:** contemporaneous intent, or that a Phase A–D set existed when construction started; that the SPEC_V2 §12 T18 gate is met; that T18-4 (issue #565) or T18-5 (issue #566) are delivered; that the V2 coverage record is current — it is stale and `build-v2-coverage.py --check` exits 1; that a project baseline, delivery contract, Phase-G compliance review or published output existed before this rework; or any closure — this pack closes nothing.

body.assignment: Rework the V2 delivery slice T18 (SPEC_V2 §10.5 and §12 T18) by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: author and publish the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the charter, the Statement of Architecture Work and the delivery contract, take the scope baseline with the one WBS deliverable, record the retrospective Phase-G compliance review, publish the expected outputs project-brief, inception-analysis and architecture-design plus the evidence output, and leave the project active because T18-4 and T18-5 are not delivered. The work is retrospective: it reconstructs the governance record from the project row, the plan, the route table and the issue registry, and it attests no contemporaneous intent.
body.scope: the shell, route registry and navigation; the ten V2 destinations of SPEC_V2 §10.5 and the execution room; the L1–L4 delivery view; one Playwright spec per destination; the V2 coverage instrument measured from apps/web/src/app.rs and the named specs; and the T12 organisation loop as the final acceptance. Out of scope: new tables, actions, events or ports; SSR, a second router or frontend, or a mobile app; retiring or rebuilding the design pack; the V1 routes, which are linked rather than re-implemented; and any production fixture or live tenant write inside the retrospective.

The Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board) approves the Phase A–D artefacts and the delivery contract. The sponsoring group is accountable for the tranche-4 authorisation and for keeping the project active. The owning slices T4, T5, T7, T9, T10, T11, T13, T16 and T17 are responsible for the actions each destination calls, and T12 owns the final organisation loop.
body.acceptance_criteria: The SPEC_V2 §12 T18 gate, judged by the fifteen checks of acceptance/programme/T18.toml: every destination route exists with its spec, each spec asserts empty, error, happy and one refusal, the coverage record reports exists only from a real route and a present spec with a *Gate reported as extend naming its owner, no production screen renders a fixture, and a signed-in tenant drives portfolio → programme → project → work package, organisation → release → binding, procedures intake → publish, tools call → ledger, improve → kata → adoption, operations incident → postmortem and the ADM phase rail from the app, with the T12 loop as the final spec.
body.contract: The delivery contract record is requested and approved live by scripts/rework-project.py under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14 and is titled 'Delivery contract — T18 The real V2 UI (retrospective, 2026-11-24)'. It commits the lane to the §12 gate and to the two open units as typed dependencies, and it records that this retrospective neither closes the project nor waives any check. The contract's approval is retrospective; the historical snapshot has no live contract, which is one of the failed checks in the prior acceptance record.

The document this catalog sits under is the T18 retrospective pack of 2026-11-24, published by scripts/rework-project.py. It is the Phase C counterpart to the Phase A solution concept: the UI is a client of the registry and the rows, not a second store, and the catalogue shows that the project's data footprint is zero new entities. artifacts.body:
# Technology Standards Catalog — T18 The real V2 UI (Phase D)

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase D; plateau hld; owner the T18 lane under the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board); review date 2026-11-24; project 01a20c80-b734-748a-b299-879ea19be681; tranche 4 id 01a1e9e0-f4c0-727d-9afb-bb5b1e9783ce; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. The standards are reconstructed from ADR 0001, ADR 0009, ADR 0013, SPEC_V2 §10.5.4 and the plan's verification section; each names an owner and a verifier that exists in the repository.

## Entries

Ten standards. The client stack stays Leptos CSR/WASM in the one binary; writes are action-only with the concurrency and approval headers; reads are literal GETs; auth is OIDC PKCE with an in-memory token; each destination has one four-state Playwright spec and web.yml is the browser gate; the coverage script is the measurement rule; the design pack is outside production; fixtures are banned; and the bundle budget is the render guard. The standards are the same ones the V1 application already follows, so T18 adds no technology choice.

## Links

Derives from ADR 0001, ADR 0009, ADR 0013, SPEC_V2 §10.5.4 and §12 T18, and docs/plans/T18-real-v2-ui.md §§5, 8 and 10. Verifiers are apps/web/src/api.rs, apps/web/src/auth.rs, apps/web/e2e, .github/workflows/web.yml, scripts/build-v2-coverage.py and acceptance/programme/T18.toml. Links the owning slices and issues #562–#566, #629 and #630; the design pack is a reference, not a standard for production code.

## Document

The document this catalog sits under is the T18 retrospective pack of 2026-11-24, published by scripts/rework-project.py. It records the Phase D standards that make the Phase B capabilities testable: the four-state spec, the action-only write, the literal-GET read and the coverage rule are the enforcement points the Phase-G review cites. It does not claim that every standard is currently green: the coverage check is red on stale output, and Tools and Architecture are gates. Project id 01a20c80-b734-748a-b299-879ea19be681.

That red record measures the pre-rework state and is the reason this pack exists; it is not evidence that the delivered screens are wrong. The delivered construction is real: apps/web/src/app.rs registers /portfolio, /portfolio/:programme_id, /programme, /organisation, /procedures, /authoring, /plan, /improve, /operations, /execution, /design/adm and /tools, with /tools and /design/adm rendering ToolsGate and AdmGate; apps/web/e2e carries shell, portfolio, programme, organisation, procedures, authoring, plan, improve, operations, execution and admin specs; and issues #559, #562, #563, #564 and #629 are closed. The remaining limits are explicit: issue #565 (T18-4) and issue #566 (T18-5) are open and issue #630 (T18-3c) is blocked; Tools has no destination spec and the architecture destination has no `adm.spec.ts` (the existing `admin.spec.ts` covers /settings/admin, not the ADM rail); docs/evidence/v2-coverage.json is stale, reporting seven destination rows as exists and four as extend (Architecture, Improve, Operations, Tools) while build-v2-coverage.py --check exits 1; the T12 organisation loop has no spec; and no project baseline, delivery contract, Phase-G review, project-brief, inception-analysis, architecture-design or evidence output was published before this pack. The level is consistent, not compliant or conformant: the evidence supports that the project is active and its construction has advanced, but it does not support the §12 gate, which is why this pack supplies the governance record and closes nothing.

# Project brief — T18 The real V2 UI (retrospective, 2026-11-24)

## Outcome

After T18 a signed-in tenant drives every V2 destination from the conveyor's own application — portfolio, programme, project and work package; organisation, release and binding; procedures intake and publish; tools call and ledger; improve, kata and adoption; operations incident and postmortem; and the ADM phase rail — while the programme measures those screens from the app's real route table and Playwright specs instead of the static design mock. At the snapshot the construction is partial: eight of the ten V2 destination routes render real screens, tools and architecture remain honest gates, and the SPEC_V2 §12 gate is not yet met.

## Boundary

In scope: the application shell and navigation, the route registry, the V2 destinations of SPEC_V2 §10.5 plus the execution room, the L1–L4 delivery view, one Playwright spec per destination, and the V2 coverage instrument measured from real routes. Out of scope: new tables, actions, events or ports; SSR, a mobile app or a second router; retiring or redesigning the design pack, which stays the public programme site at `/design/` and the reviewed reference (D64); the V1 routes, which are linked and not re-implemented; and any live tenant write or production fixture inside a pull request.

## Reuse sources

Reuse `apps/web/src/app.rs` (router, sidebar and top bar), `api.rs` (If-Match, Idempotency-Key and approval-id request shapes), `auth.rs` (OIDC PKCE with an in-memory token), `state.rs` (tenant, me and manifest signals), `sse.rs`, `components.rs` and `palette.rs`; the existing screen modules and V1 specs; the e2e harness (`fixture.ts`, `dev-server.mjs`, `playwright.config.ts`) and `web.yml`; the compiled action registry of SPEC_V2 §10.4; `docs/design/v2.js` and `STUDIO-SPEC.md` as the reviewed design reference; and the programme, work and measure read models exposed by the owning slices.

## Inception units

The project starts from the inception analysis at `docs/plans/T18/inception-analysis.md` and the architecture design at `docs/plans/T18/architecture-design.md`. The analysis measures the starting state at `main@490ad555`: 31 routes, 25 screen modules and 31 specs, all V1, and no `/portfolio`, `/programme`, `/organisation`, `/procedures`, `/authoring`, `/plan`, `/improve`, `/operations`, `/tools` or `/design/adm` route. The design fixes the destination read and write contracts, the D64/D65 decisions, the single-writer router constraint and the rule that a missing backend capability is a typed dependency, not a local fetch.

## Dependencies

Construction is blocked-by T0, T1, T2, T3 and P0 — the model and contracts, the plan spine, the decision ladder, the PM job and the programme definition. Acceptance is blocked-by T4, T5, T7, T9, T10, T11, T13, T16 and T17, because each destination's live scenarios wait on its owning slice, and by T12, whose organisation loop is driven from the UI as the final spec. Issue #526 is related: its generated record is rebased and regenerated, never hand-merged. While a slice is absent the destination renders not yet live and names the owner rather than inventing a fetch.

## Acceptance

The SPEC_V2 §12 T18 gate requires that every destination route exists with its Playwright spec; that a signed-in tenant drives the portfolio → programme → project → work-package, organisation → release → binding, procedures intake → publish, tools call → ledger, improve → kata → adoption, operations incident → postmortem and ADM phase-rail paths from the app; that every destination spec asserts empty, error, happy and one refusal; that the V2 coverage record reports exists only from a real route and its spec; and that no production screen renders a fixture. `acceptance/programme/T18.toml` carries the fifteen gate checks, including project, baseline, contract, review, WSJF, demo credits, coverage, artefact-standard and rework resolution.

## Capabilities

The tenant operator who runs the portfolio, programme, plan, organisation, procedures, authoring, tools, improve, operations and architecture surfaces owns the outcome, with the PM, kanban-coach, kata, development and operations jobs those destinations serve. The UI is their surface, not a new job: it exposes the action families that T0–T17 own, and the seven nav groups are trimmed to destinations that exist and gated by `has_action`. The delivery view gives the sponsoring group and the SRO one L1–L4 line from portfolio to work package, with spend read from the ledger rather than fabricated.

## Plan

The project is held to `docs/plans/T18-real-v2-ui.md`, SPEC_V2 §10.5 (the real-UI route table) and §12 T18 (the gate), with ADR 0013 recording that the real UI is the app and not the design pack. The five sequenced units are issues #562 (shell, route registry, portfolio, programme and the delivery view), #563 (organisation, jobs, agents, decisions, project types, plan and validation), #564 (procedures, capabilities, authoring, execution and run history), #565 (tools, metering, operations and improve) and #566 (architecture, system architecture, knowledge, measure and the T12 acceptance). #565 and #566 remain open at this snapshot.

# Evidence — T18 The real V2 UI (retrospective, 2026-11-24)

## Claim

T18's retrospective record is consistent with the construction actually present in `apps/web`: the shell, portfolio, programme, organisation, procedures, authoring, plan, improve, operations and execution surfaces are real routes with screen modules and Playwright specs, while tools and the ADM phase rail remain honest gates, two delivery units are still open, and the SPEC_V2 §12 T18 gate is therefore not met. This pack supplies the missing Phase A–D artefacts, the Statement of Architecture Work, the delivery contract and the retrospective Phase-G review; it closes nothing and leaves the project active.

## Evidence

Measured in the worktree on 2026-11-24: `apps/web/src/app.rs` registers `/portfolio`, `/portfolio/:programme_id`, `/programme`, `/organisation`, `/procedures`, `/authoring`, `/plan`, `/improve`, `/operations`, `/execution`, `/design/adm` and `/tools`, with `/tools` and `/design/adm` rendering `ToolsGate` and `AdmGate`. `apps/web/e2e` carries `shell.spec.ts`, `portfolio.spec.ts`, `programme.spec.ts`, `organisation.spec.ts`, `procedures.spec.ts`, `authoring.spec.ts`, `plan.spec.ts`, `improve.spec.ts`, `operations.spec.ts`, `execution.spec.ts` and `admin.spec.ts`. Issues #559, #562, #563, #564 and #629 are closed; #565 (T18-4) and #566 (T18-5) are open and #630 (T18-3c) is blocked. The project-acceptance record `docs/evidence/rework/T18.json` (2026-11-24T21:07:28Z) is red with nine failed checks, and `docs/evidence/v2-coverage.json` is stale: it reports seven destination rows `exists` and four `extend` (Architecture, Improve, Operations, Tools).

## Verification

An independent reader can repeat the check. Run `grep -n 'path!' apps/web/src/app.rs` to see the route table; run `ls apps/web/e2e/*.spec.ts` to see the destination specs; run `python3 scripts/build-v2-coverage.py --check`, which currently exits 1 on stale output and must be regenerated before the coverage claim can be green; run `python3 scripts/acceptance.py --manifest acceptance/programme/T18.toml` to reproduce the project-acceptance result; and run `python3 scripts/rework-content-check.py --project T18 --content docs/evidence/rework/tranche-4/rework-content-T18.json --snapshot /tmp/conv526-w1-snap/data --wsjf 9,7,10,5 --closes false` to verify this pack before publication. Each command reads the repository or the retained snapshot and makes no governance write.

## Links

SPEC_V2 §10.5 and §12 T18; `docs/plans/T18-real-v2-ui.md`; `docs/plans/T18/project-brief.md`, `inception-analysis.md` and `architecture-design.md`; `docs/decisions/0013-real-v2-ui.md`; `acceptance/programme/T18.toml`; `docs/evidence/rework/T18.json`; `docs/evidence/v2-coverage.json`; issues #559 and #562–#566; the tranche-4 authorisation `01a1e9e0-f4c0-727d-9afb-bb5b1e9783ce` and the tranche-3 review `01a20e84-325b-7fef-8f40-50b5e53550e9`; the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`.

## Gap

Not evidenced: that the SPEC_V2 §12 T18 gate is met; that T18-4 and T18-5 are delivered; that the T12 organisation loop runs from the UI; that the coverage record is current — it is stale and the check is red; that a project baseline, delivery contract, Phase-G review or published output existed before this retrospective; and any closure. Tools and the ADM rail are gates without destination specs, the project row remains `status: active` with `measured_status: proposed`, and the two open delivery units are acceptance-blocked-by their owning slices. The metering destination has no route at this snapshot, and the execution room names the executor-kind, binding-pin and tool-ledger gaps rather than hiding them.
